description_open: The sand is sliding under a trap-jaw ant. With no steady foothold, it snaps its jaws into the slope—and lifts off.
How does a bite become a jump? Follow Odontomachus brunneus into an antlion pit, see why one launch falls short, and watch how researchers tested whether being able to snap helps an ant escape.

chapters.title: What turns a snap into a jump?

disclosure: Cinematic CGI based on published research, not field footage or measured strike timing. The cover is illustrative artwork. Foley and score are designed, not recordings of insects.
references: Larabee & Suarez (2015) — antlion encounters and jaw-restraint experiment: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0124871
Sutton et al. (2022) — dual-spring jaw mechanism: https://doi.org/10.1242/jeb.244077
Büsse et al. (2021) — sand-pit maintenance, studied in a different antlion species: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8440033/
